previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a paraplegic woman with a history of recurrent pneumonias and UTIs, was admitted for hypoxia and productive cough. She was found to have Klebsiella pneumonia and sepsis, requiring intubation and pressor support. After initial improvement, she was extubated but developed right lung collapse and pleuritic pain. She later requested re-intubation due to worsening dyspnea, during which she suffered a PEA arrest likely due to airway plugging. She was resuscitated, underwent bronchoscopy, and was stabilized. A tracheostomy was placed, and she gradually improved with minimal ventilator support. Her anemia remained stable, and she was discharged to extended care on trach mask with a Dobhoff tube, awake and alert.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F paraplegic with a hx of recurrent UTIs, PNAs, sepsis, 
presenting with 3 days of UTI (with + urine culture) and 
worsening productive cough/hypoxia likely representing PNA, who 
developed PRES in ICU setting. 
.  
# PNA: Patient presented in hypoxic & hypercapneic respiratory 
failure, requiring intubation in ED. CXR was notable for 
pulmonary vascular congestion with possible focal areas of 
infiltrate in the LUL and RML. Patient received empiric 
vanco/zosyn. She briefly required levophed, which was weaned at 
arrival to the MICU. Given recent hospitalization in ___ and 
MRSA in sputum, she was treated for healthcare associated PNA, 
as well as for UTI, with vancomycin, meropenema and gentamycin. 
She completed a 7 day course of vanco and gent, and 14 d of 
meropenem.
On ___, she was extubated, but given her sedation and 
incresed work of breathing, she was reintubated.  The 
possibility of a tracheostomy was raised but apparently the 
patient refused.  
The patient was educated about good airway clearance. She 
received chest ___ and was able to provide good coughing on her 
own. 02 sat was 94-95% on room air at discharge. 
.  
#PRES:  Patient became hypertensive to the 180s in the MICU 
setting and was started on IV hydralazine. On ___, she 
developed a severe headache with binocular blindness and 
decreased facial sensation in the setting of high blood 
pressures; CT and MRI were consistent with diagnosis of PRES 
syndrome.  Neurology was consulted who recommended a blood 
pressure between 120 and 140.  Chlorthalidone was started and BP 
remained largely within goal range, with some blood pressure in 
90-100s. Headache and vision greatly improved by discharge. 
Neurology recommended follow-up MRI in 2 weeks and ___ clinic, 
as well as ___ clinic appointments. The patient was instructed 
to continue chlorthalidone and check BP at home twice daily. Dr. 
___ neurology ___ determine need for continued 
antihypertensives at home. 
.
# UTI: Patient has h/o recurrent UTI ___ self-catheterization. 
Urine culture Citrobacter Freundii, sensitive to Meropenem with 
MIC < 4. ID recommended meropenem and gentamycin for synergy. 
Completed 14 day course.  
.  
# ANEMIA: Stable. History of anemia of chronic disease. No 
transfusions required.
.  
# S/p traumatic spine injury/chronic pain: Initially held 
methadone, oxycodone, oxybutynin, Klonapin. All meds restarted 
prior to discharge.
.  
# Hypothyroidism: continued home levothyroxine  
.
# Hepatitis C: negative VL recently

Discharge Instructions:
It was a pleasure taking care of you. You were admitted for 
urinary tract infection and pneumonia. You required intubation 
for the pneumonia. You are at especially high risk for pneumonia 
and should work on deep breathing and good coughing to clear 
your lungs. You received antibiotics and improved.
You also had a syndrome called PRES, which caused vision loss 
and headache. This occurred because your blood pressure 
increased causing swelling in the back of your brain. This 
syndrome gets better on its own and you will follow up with 
neurology and opthalmology to make sure you completely recover. 
You will need another MRI in 2 weeks. You will continue to take 
chlorthalidone to control your blood pressure until you see Dr.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  A ___ female with hypoxia and hypotension.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs available from ___.

Portable supine AP view of the chest.  Again there are bibasilar opacities,
unchanged from prior chest radiograph, consistent with persistent pulmonary
edema secondary to CHF.  There is stable cardiomegaly, with prominence of the
pulmonary vasculature.  There is no pneumothorax.  There is slight blunting of
the costophrenic angles, likely due to small pleural effusions.  Overall,
there is relatively little change from the prior radiograph.  Again there is
surgical hardware within the left humerus. There are stable defomities of the
right ribcage, seen prior exams. 

IMPRESSION:  
1. Persistent bibasilar opacities and stable cardiomegaly, consistent with
mild CHF.  An underlying pneumonia cannot be excluded. 
2. Bilateral pleural effusions.

INDICATION:  ___ female with presumed sepsis, status post central line
placement via the right IJ.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph available from ___ at 11:16 a.m.

PORTABLE SUPINE AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  There is a new central line placed via
the right IJ, terminating within the lower SVC.  There has been interval
increase in degree of opacification within the lungs, most significantly
within the left upper lobe, concerning for worsening pulmonary edema or
interval aspiration.  The other aspects of the examination are unchanged since
the prior film from the same date.

IMPRESSION: 
1)  Status post right IJ central line, terminating in the lower SVC. 
2)  Increased pulmonary opacities, left greater than right, concerning for
pulmonary edema or aspiration.

INDICATION:  ___ female with overload and pneumonia, status post
intubation.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph available from ___.

PORTABLE SUPINE AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  Patient is status post intubation.  The
endotracheal tube is positioned 3.8 cm above the level of the carina.  Again
there is a central line terminating within the lower SVC.  There has been
interval improvement of the bilateral pulmonary opacity since the 12:45 chest
radiograph exam, as well as better definition of the costophrenic angles.  The
other aspects of the examination are unchanged.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Status post endotracheal tube placement, terminating 3.8 cm above the
level of the carina.
2.  Interval improvement of the bilateral pulmonary aeration.

HISTORY:  Fluid overload.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is increasing
opacification, especially involving the left hemithorax and primarily the left
base.  Although there may be some element of elevated pulmonary venous
pressure and chronic lung disease, the current appearance is consistent with
pneumonia.

Endotracheal tube and nasogastric tube remain in standard position.  Right IJ
catheter has been pushed forward so that the tip lies in the lower SVC.

LIMITED ABDOMINAL SONOGRAM

INDICATION:  ___ woman with prior ascites, admitted with sepsis.

COMPARISON:  No recent studies are available for direct comparison.

FINDINGS:  Targeted scanning of four abdominal quadrants demonstrates trace
perihepatic ascites.

IMPRESSION:  Trace perihepatic ascites.

PROCEDURE:  Chest portable AP.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Pneumonia, intubated.

FINDINGS: In comparison to the previous chest radiograph ,symmetrical
bilateral pulmonary edema is now severe, bilateral pleural effusions are
unchanged and severe cardiomegaly is stable.  The tip of the ET tube is 37 mm
above the carina with unchanged overdistention of the cuff, NG tube passes
into the stomach and out of view.  Right central venous catheter unchanged,
the tip in the right atrium.

IMPRESSION:  Worsening pulmonary edema which is now severe with presence of
cardiomegaly and small bilateral pleural effusions.  Overdistention of the ET
cuff is similar to the previous chest radiograph.  MICU7 contacted.

SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Pneumonia.

Comparison is made with prior study performed a day earlier.

Moderate cardiomegaly is unchanged.  ET tube, NG tube, and right IJ remain in
place in standard position.  Diffuse lung consolidations that are more
prominent in the mid lower lungs have minimally improved and consistent with
improving pulmonary edema.  Small bilateral pleural effusions earlier on the
right side are unchanged.

SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Respiratory failure in intubated patient.

Comparison is made with prior studies including ___.

Moderate cardiomegaly is stable.  There has been minimally improvement of
pulmonary edema.  Small bilateral pleural effusions are unchanged associated
with adjacent atelectasis.  ET tube, right IJ and NG tube remain in place. 
There is no pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  Respiratory failure.

FINDINGS:  AP semi-upright chest radiograph is compared with ___.  The endotracheal tube terminates 3.5 cm from the carina.  The
orogastric tube terminates beneath the diaphragm.  The right central venous
catheter terminates in the lower SVC.  There are unchanged increased
interstitial markings.  There is moderate cardiomegaly.  There is minimal
increased aeration at the left lung base.  There are continued small bilateral
pleural effusions with atelectasis.

SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Respiratory failure and intubated patient.

Comparison is made with prior study performed a day earlier.

Increased opacity in the left lower lobe worsening from prior study could be
just due to difference in positioning of the patient and shifting of the
pleural effusion and adjacent atelectasis.  Otherwise cardiomegaly and
increase in the interstitial markings due to pulmonary edema sparring the
right upper lobe are stable.  Lines and tubes remain in place in standard
position.  Right pleural effusion and adjacent atelectasis is stable.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with pneumonia, intubated.

Portable AP chest radiograph was compared to ___ obtained at
05:42 a.m.

The ET tube tip remains low, approximately 2.8 cm above the carina but at
least in part may be related to flexion of patient's neck.  The NG tube tip is
in the stomach.  The right internal jugular line tip is at the low SVC. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged including moderate to severe
cardiomegaly.  The bilateral consolidations, left more than right are
unchanged.  No evidence of pneumothorax is seen.  Small bilateral pleural
effusions are unchanged.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  Radiograph of earlier the same date.

INDICATION:  Feeding tube placement.

FINDINGS:  Nasogastric tube has been either repositioned or replaced and now
coils within the stomach.  No feeding tube is identified.  Other indwelling
devices remain in place, with slight repositioning of endotracheal tube, which
now terminates about 5 cm above the carina.  Cardiac silhouette remains
enlarged.  Improving bilateral perihilar and basilar consolidation.  Such
rapid improvement favors pulmonary edema, but pneumonia may still contribute
to remaining areas of abnormal opacification.  Small pleural effusions, left
greater than right, are unchanged.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  Study earlier the same date.

INDICATION:  Acute respiratory change.

FINDINGS:  Allowing for technical differences between the studies, there has
been little change since the recent radiograph of several hours earlier,
except for slight improved aeration in the left base manifested by improved
visualization of the left hemidiaphragm.  Indwelling devices remain in
standard position, but cuff of the endotracheal tube, maybe slightly
overdistended.

PROCEDURE:  Chest portable AP.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  Bilateral pleural effusions are small and probably unchanged as the
patient is currently supine. The perihilar and lower lobe opacities are
essentially unchanged since the previous chest radiograph, probably due to a
combination of layering pleural effusions with pulmonary edema.
The ET tube, NG tube, right central venous line is unchanged in position.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral pleural effusions with bilateral perihilar and lower lobe opacities
and most likely edema, although there could be superimposed consolidation in
the right lung base.

INDICATION:  Assess interval change in this patient who was reintubated for
respiratory distress and has a history of pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___, and ___.

SINGLE AP SUPINE CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  No significant change in bilateral
perihilar and basilar opacities.  Pleural effusions if any may be small. 
Endotracheal tube is in satisfactory position, with distention of the
endotracheal tube cuff.  Right IJ central venous catheter terminates in the
mid-to-low SVC.  There is no evidence of pneumothorax.  The cardiac size is in
the upper limits of normal.  The hilar and mediastinal contours are normal.

The ___ tube courses through the stomach and out of view.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Unchanged mild-to-moderate pulmonary edema.
2.  Over-distention of the endotracheal tube cuff .

ROUTINE UNENHANCED CT HEAD

HISTORY:  Headaches and blindness.

Comparison is made with ___.

FINDINGS:
There is hypodensity in the posterior parietal lobes bilaterally, left greater
than right.  In the setting of underlying hypertension, this could represent
PRES.  MRI can be performed for further evaluation if clinically indicated.
Otherwise, there is no evidence of acute hemorrhage, midline shift, or mass
effect.

Evaluation of the remaining brain demonstrates no significant abnormality.  No
bony lesion is identified.

IMPRESSION:
Mild posterior white matter hypodensities as described.  In the appropriate
clinical setting, this may be manifestation of PRES.  Recommend correlation
with MRI.

EXAM:  MRI brain.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Patient with new-onset sensory deficits and blindness.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and FLAIR T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial images
of the brain were acquired.  Correlation was made with the CT of ___.

FINDINGS:  There are bilateral confluent areas of hyperintensities seen in the
parietooccipital lobes and a small focus of hyperintensity is seen in the left
thalamus consistent with posterior reversible encephalopathy.  No evidence of
restricted diffusion seen in these regions.  There is no midline shift or
hydrocephalus.  Mild-to-moderate brain atrophy is seen.  Suprasellar and
craniocervical regions are normal on the sagittal images.  The vascular flow
voids are maintained.  Small amount of fluid is seen in the left mastoid air
cells.

IMPRESSION:  Bilateral parietooccipital white matter hyperintensities also
involving gray matter consistent with posterior reversible encephalopathy.  No
evidence of restricted diffusion seen.
